title: Why Blackbirds Search the Grass and Sing at Dawn

narration_timeline.text: Why is this common blackbird pulling something from the grass instead of singing?
narration_timeline.scene: Close blackbird visibly carrying a worm and foraging in botanical garden.

narration_timeline.text: In gardens and parks, blackbirds often search low vegetation for food.
narration_timeline.scene: Close blackbird resting on rocky park ground.

narration_timeline.text: One bird walks through green plants, then moves on to check another small patch.
narration_timeline.scene: Two real blackbird park scenes in Ljubljana.

narration_timeline.text: That ground search can uncover insects, worms, and other small things a blackbird eats.
narration_timeline.scene: Blackbird in Tivoli park; food type explained without fake closeup.

narration_timeline.text: At dawn, the same species may sing from a perch before returning to daytime routines.
narration_timeline.scene: Actual dark predawn blackbird singing on rooftop antenna, clearly marked dawn.

narration_timeline.text: So a blackbird's day shifts between finding food on the ground and sending song across its habitat.
narration_timeline.scene: Two separate blackbird ground-level park/city scenes.
